findings.title: Breaking change: recreate-upgrade exit code changed from 4 to 3
findings.body: RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE was changed from 4 to 3 to free up exit code 4 for the new FEATURE_DISABLED case. This silently changes the public CLI contract of `kc.sh update-compatibility check` for any existing user. Pipelines/scripts that detect a required recreate upgrade by checking `if [ $? -eq 4 ]` will no longer match and will incorrectly conclude the deployment succeeded or that the feature was disabled. Because the PR description does not call this out as a breaking change and the docs are updated as if the new mapping was always in effect, users upgrading will be broken without warning. The change should either be reverted (keep 4 for recreate and pick another code for FEATURE_DISABLED, e.g. 5) or prominently documented as a breaking change in the release notes.

findings.title: No test for `update-compatibility check` when the rolling-updates feature is disabled
findings.body: The new `testFeatureNotEnabled` only exercises `update-compatibility metadata` without enabling the feature. The matching code path in `UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run()` that prints `printFeatureDisabled()` and exits with `CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED` (=4) is left uncovered. A symmetric test such as `@Launch({UpdateCompatibility.NAME, UpdateCompatibilityCheck.NAME})` asserting the same error message would lock in the contract for both subcommands and prevent one of them silently regressing.

findings.title: CAUTION overstates behavior: operator does not fail when feature is disabled unless spec.update.strategy is set
findings.body: The CAUTION says "While on preview stage, the feature `rolling-updates` must be enabled. Otherwise, the {project_name} Operator will fail." This is misleading: the operator still functions with the default (legacy) update strategy when the feature is not enabled, as demonstrated by `UpgradeTest.createInitialDeployment` whose `updateStrategy == null` branch returns the Keycloak CR without enabling the feature and the test still passes. The wording should clarify that the feature is only required when the user sets `spec.update.strategy`; otherwise readers may believe enabling rolling-updates is mandatory for any Keycloak deployment.

findings.title: CAUTION removed the prior TODO without leaving context for readers
findings.body: The diff replaces a one-line `// TODO Link to discussion?` comment with a CAUTION block. While the new CAUTION is informative, it does not link to or mention the discussion referenced by `previewDiscussionLink` (keycloak/keycloak#36785), even though the discussion is the canonical place for users to give feedback while the command is preview. Either keep a pointer to the discussion or rely on `previewDiscussionLink` already being rendered at the top of the page, but ensure the CAUTION does not inadvertently hide the feedback channel from users experimenting with the tool.
